examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: Ichidan verb: blunt imperative 見ろ ('look!') is rough command speech.
Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.en: that (near the listener or just mentioned)
meanings.note: Must always precede a noun (その椅子 'that chair').

examples.text: 仮に女優が見つかったとしても、その委員会が許可しねえと販売できねえってことか。
examples.trans: So even if we somehow found an actress, we can't sell a tape unless that commission approves it?

examples.text: でも、委員会の規制を守らないかぎり作品は出せませんよ。
examples.trans: Even so, unless we abide by the commission's regulations, we won't be able to release the film.

examples.text: 委員会さえクリアすりゃ、今ならいくらでも店に置いてやるぞ。
examples.trans: As long as you clear the commission, I'll stock as many copies in my stores as you want.

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.

できる.gloss: be built; open; be able to

meanings.en: come into existence; be completed; can do
meanings.note: With buildings or stores (店ができる), means a new shop has been built or opened.

examples.text: 駅前に新しいカフェができました。
examples.trans: A new café opened in front of the station.

examples.text: 日本語が少しできます。
examples.trans: I can speak a little Japanese.

meanings.note: Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.

examples.trans: We are boxed in from every direction.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
Calls someone's attention ('look here!') or asks for a brief pause (ちょっと待って).

examples.text: ちょっと待ってください。
ちょっと見てください。

meanings.note: Filler or polite attention-getter.

examples.text: あの、ちょっとよろしいですか。
examples.trans: Excuse me, do you have a moment?

examples.text: あの、実は相談があります。
examples.trans: Um, actually I have something to ask you.

examples.text: ちょっと誰だ、あのお嬢さん？
examples.trans: Hold on — who is that proper young lady over there?

examples.text: もうやめときなって。君みたいな真面目なお嬢さんがいられるとこじゃないのよ。
examples.trans: Forget it while you can — this is no place for an earnest young lady like you.

meanings.note: Used both to answer yes politely and when handing an item to someone.
Covers everything from a casual chat to a business deal or idea.

examples.trans: Let us have a little talk.

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
In もういい, means 'already enough' or 'ready now'.

meanings.en: bring to a halt; shut off
meanings.note: Transitive verb for stopping a car, engine, or machine.

examples.text: ここに車を止めてください。
エンジンを止めました。

meanings.note: Expresses change of state, or in polite customer service (になります) states an arrangement or price total.

examples.trans: That comes to one thousand yen.

meanings.note: Second-person pronoun used by superiors, in songs/books, or between close friends.

examples.text: 君の意見はどうですか。
君ならきっとできるよ。

meanings.note: Auxiliary na-adjective expressing resemblance or conjecture.

examples.trans: It looks like it's going to rain.

examples.text: 彼は忙しいみたいですね。
もうやめときなって。君みたいな真面目なお嬢さんがいられるとこじゃないのよ。
examples.trans: Forget it while you can — this is no place for an earnest young lady like you.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Marks the presence of a person (責任者はいるか) or follows て-form (often contracted to てる/てます in speech).
Attaches to the irrealis (a-stem) of godan verbs.

examples.trans: I was called by the teacher.

meanings.en: short casual form of じゃあ / では
meanings.note: Brisk spoken transition before taking the next step.
Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
I-adjective; after て-form (～てほしい), means 'want someone to do something'.

examples.trans: I want you to come soon.

examples.text: 諦めてほしくないのです。
examples.trans: I don't want you to give up.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Expresses sudden surprise, shock, or disbelief.

examples.text: えっ、もう帰るんですか。
examples.trans: Huh, are you going home already?

meanings.note: Irregular i-adjective whose past/conditional stems use よ- (よかったら).

examples.text: よかったら来てください。

meanings.note: Plural of 俺 (おれ) with pluralizing suffix ら.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.

examples.trans: If you can't decide now, let's think about it later.

meanings.en: go forward; work out well (いけます = 'it will work!')
meanings.note: Written in kana for figurative headway: いけます! ('this can go / this will work!'), 思いどおりにいかない ('does not go as hoped').

examples.text: この企画ならいけます！
examples.trans: With this plan, it will work!

examples.text: 仕事がうまくいっています。

meanings.note: Attaches to pronouns or people nouns (僕ら, 彼ら).
Contracts では; launches a decision ('well then') or opens casual farewell じゃあね.

meanings.en: come; go do something and return (after て-form)
meanings.note: Written in kana after a て-form (話してきます), expresses stepping away to do an action and coming back.

examples.text: ちょっと水を買ってきます。
examples.trans: I will go buy some water and be right back.

meanings.note: Polite/dialectal negative ending, especially in ～ません.
